4. Embedded Toric Resolution
The rational double point singularities are given by one of the following equations:
An : f(x, y, z) = xy −zn+1,
n ∈N
Dn : f(x, y, z) = z2 −x(y2 + xn−2),
n ∈N, n ≥4
E6 : f(x, y, z) = z2 + y3 + x4
E7 : f(x, y, z) = x2 + y3 + yz3
E8 : f(x, y, z) = z2 + y3 + x5
Remark 4.1. Each member of ADE-singularities is Newton non-degenerate.
Embedded toric resolutions of ADE-singularities were studied in [18, 19]. Here
differently we construct regular refinements of Gr¨obner fans of each members of
them. This leads us their embedded toric resolutions [1, 2]. Additionally, these
resolutions will be minimal which means that:
Definition 4.2. An embedded toric resolution is called minimal if
i) The vectors in the regular refinement are irreducible.
ii) The resolution graph obtaining from the refinement does not have any −1
curve means the self-intersection of each vertex is different from −1 (this gives us
the resolution graph is minimal).
Note that the self-intersection of a vertex is computed as: The number −s ∈Z≤0
with s.v = Pm
i=1 vi is called the self-intersection of the vertex v in the graph where
each vi is adjacent to v in the regular refinement.
4.1. An-singularities. Consider the hypersurface X = V (f) ⊂C3 where
f(x, y, z) = xy −zn+1,
n ∈N
Given v1 ∈(R≥0)3, let Inv1(f) = f. The polyhedral cone associated with v1 is
Cv1(f) = ⟨(n + 1, 0, 1), (0, n + 1, 1)⟩
Given v2 ∈(R≥0)3, let Inv2(f) = xy. The polyhedral cone associated with v2 is
Cv2(f) = ⟨(0, 0, 1), (n + 1, 0, 1), (0, n + 1, 1)⟩
Given v3 ∈(R≥0)3, let Inv3(f) = −zn+1. The polyhedral cone associated with v3
is
Cv3(f) = ⟨(1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), (n + 1, 0, 1), (0, n + 1, 1)⟩
